Issue Management Commands.name: AddCommentToIssue
Issue Management Commands.description: Adds a new comment to the specified issue.

Issue Management Commands.name: AttachElementsToIssue
Issue Management Commands.description: Attaches elements to the specified issue.

Issue Management Commands.name: DetachElementsFromIssue
Issue Management Commands.description: Detaches elements from the specified issue.

Issue Management Commands.name: ExportIssuesToBCF
Issue Management Commands.description: Exports specified issues to a BCF file.

Issue Management Commands.name: GetCommentsFromIssue
Issue Management Commands.description: Retrieves comments information from the specified issue.

Issue Management Commands.name: GetElementsAttachedToIssue
Issue Management Commands.description: Retrieves attached elements of the specified issue, filtered by attachment type.

Issue Management Commands.name: ImportIssuesFromBCF
Issue Management Commands.description: Imports issues from the specified BCF file.

Issue Management Commands.name: ImportMarkupsFromPDF
Issue Management Commands.description: Imports the markups of the specified PDF file as issues, like Issue Manager > Import PDF markups, without any dialog and without opening the Issue Manager palette, and reports the issues it created. Available from Archicad 29.

Library Commands.name: AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary
Library Commands.description: Adds the given files into the embedded library. With the overwriteExisting flag an embedded library item already existing on an outputPath is replaced (Archicad 27 or newer).

Library Commands.name: AddLibraries
Library Commands.description: Adds the given folders to the project's local libraries, skipping any already loaded.

Library Commands.name: CopyFilesIntoEmbeddedLibrary
Library Commands.description: Copies the given files, keeping their names, into a folder of the embedded library with one library operation. The target folder is created when it is missing. With overwriteIfExists an item of the same name in that folder is replaced.

Library Commands.name: CreateFolderInEmbeddedLibrary
Library Commands.description: Creates a folder, with any missing parent folders, inside the embedded library. The folderPath is relative to the embedded library, like the outputPath of AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary.

Library Commands.name: DeleteEmbeddedLibraryItems
Library Commands.description: Deletes the given items from the embedded library. The path of an item is the same relative path that AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary takes as outputPath. Available from Archicad 27.

Library Commands.name: GetAvailableLibraryParts
Library Commands.description: Lists library parts currently available to the project. Filter by typeId (e.g. 'Door', 'Window', 'Object', 'Lamp').

Library Commands.name: GetLibraries
Library Commands.description: Gets the list of loaded libraries.

Library Commands.name: SetLibraries
Library Commands.description: Makes the given folders the project's local libraries; built-in, embedded, server and web libraries are kept. Set the libraries before opening a file that needs them and the missing-library dialog does not appear.

Library Commands.name: SetLibraryPartScripts
Library Commands.description: Sets the master, parameter, 2D, 3D and properties scripts of loaded library parts. Only the given scripts are changed; an empty script makes the section empty. A library part that is not editable (e.g. a part of a library package or a read-only library) is refused and left unchanged. Available from Archicad 28.

Property Commands.name: AddPropertyToAttributes
Property Commands.description: Makes an existing custom property available for the given attributes (for example Building Materials), in one undo step. Available in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 only.

Property Commands.name: CreatePropertyDefinitions
Property Commands.description: Creates Custom Property Definitions based on the given parameters.

Property Commands.name: CreatePropertyGroups
Property Commands.description: Creates Property Groups based on the given parameters.

Property Commands.name: DeletePropertyDefinitions
Property Commands.description: Deletes the given Custom Property Definitions.

Property Commands.name: DeletePropertyGroups
Property Commands.description: Deletes the given Custom Property Groups.

Property Commands.name: GetAllProperties
Property Commands.description: Returns all user defined and built-in properties.

Property Commands.name: GetPropertyDefinitionsOfAttributes
Property Commands.description: Returns the property definitions of the given attributes (for example Building Materials): the user defined, the fundamental built-in, or all of them.

Property Commands.name: GetPropertyValuesOfAttributes
Property Commands.description: Returns the property values of the attributes for the given property.

Property Commands.name: GetPropertyValuesOfElements
Property Commands.description: Returns the property values of the elements for the given property. It works for subelements of hierarchal elements also. With includeAvailability it also tells whether each property is available for the element.

Property Commands.name: ImportPropertiesXml
Property Commands.description: Imports a Property Manager XML export, with the given policy for names that already exist. Returns the property definitions it created and removed.

Property Commands.name: MakePropertyAvailableForElements
Property Commands.description: Makes a property definition available for all the given elements. Available only in Archicad 27.

Property Commands.name: MakePropertyUnavailableForElements
Property Commands.description: Makes a property definition unavailable for all the given elements. Available only in Archicad 27.

Property Commands.name: RemovePropertyFromAttributes
Property Commands.description: Makes a custom property unavailable for the given attributes (for example Building Materials), in one undo step. Available in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 only.

Property Commands.name: SetPropertyValuesOfAttributes
Property Commands.description: Sets the property values of attributes.

Property Commands.name: SetPropertyValuesOfElements
Property Commands.description: Sets the property values of elements. It works for subelements of hierarchal elements also.

Property Commands.name: UpdatePropertyDefinitions
Property Commands.description: Updates existing Custom Property Definitions in place, keeping their guid: name, description, group, default value or expressions, availability, and enum options (add, rename, remove, reorder).

Property Commands.name: UpdatePropertyGroups
Property Commands.description: Updates the name and/or description of existing Custom Property Groups, keeping their guid.

Favorites Commands.name: ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults
Favorites Commands.description: Apply the given favorites to element defaults.

Favorites Commands.name: ApplyFavoritesToElements
Favorites Commands.description: Apply the given favorites to existing elements. Only settings-type parameters are changed - geometry (position, floor, and dimensions such as a Wall's height) is left untouched, so applying a Favorite never moves or resizes the target element. For the hierarchical types (Stair, Railing, Curtain Wall) the settings of the sub-elements are not applied, because they are inseparable from the Favorite's own geometry. By default settings, classifications, categories and properties are all applied; each can be opted out of individually. keepFields lists fields of the target (its ID, layer, an opening's width, height and sill height, a Wall's reference line location, height and top link) that are copied back after the Favorite has been applied, so that e.g. only the library part or the wall type changes.

Favorites Commands.name: CreateFavoritesFromElements
Favorites Commands.description: Create favorites from the given elements.

Favorites Commands.name: ExportFavorites
Favorites Commands.description: Export the project's Favorites to a .prefs file or folder. From Archicad 29 they can also be exported to a folder of Favorite files (xml format) or to a legacy .prf file (legacyPRF format).

Favorites Commands.name: GetAllFavorites
Favorites Commands.description: Returns every Favorite of the project, or only those of the given element type, with its name and element type. Available from Archicad 29.

Favorites Commands.name: GetFavoritePreviewImage
Favorites Commands.description: Returns the preview image of the given favorite.

Favorites Commands.name: GetFavoriteSettings
Favorites Commands.description: Reads the stored settings of the given favorites without applying them or placing an element: the element type, the folder, the library part and GDL parameters, the marker (library part and parameters) of Window and Door favorites, and the sub-elements. A favorite without a marker has no marker field, which is not an error. The other settings of the element (pens, layer, structure, etc.) are not returned.

Favorites Commands.name: GetFavoritesByType
Favorites Commands.description: Returns a list of the names of all favorites with the given element type

Favorites Commands.name: ImportFavorites
Favorites Commands.description: Import Favorites from a .prefs file or folder into the current project.

Favorites Commands.name: UpdateFavoritesFromElements
Favorites Commands.description: Update existing favorites from the given elements.

Navigator Commands.name: Change3DStyles
Navigator Commands.description: Changes the given fields of existing 3D styles, identified by name. Available from Archicad 27.

Navigator Commands.name: ChangeDrawingLink
Navigator Commands.description: Relinks a Drawing to a different source navigator item. Archicad has no in-place relink API, so this recreates the Drawing against the new source and deletes the original - the returned elementId is a NEW guid, not the input one. The Drawing Title marker's own position is not preserved (undocumented Archicad limitation). The new source view is made current before the Drawing is created (Archicad 27 or later), and the window and story that were active when the command started are restored afterwards; the view settings (zoom, layers, scale) shown in that window are not restored.

Navigator Commands.name: CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap
Navigator Commands.description: Clones Project Map viewpoints into a specified View Map folder.

Navigator Commands.name: Create3DStyles
Navigator Commands.description: Creates 3D styles. Each new style starts from the current 3D style and differs from it only in the given fields. Available from Archicad 27.

Navigator Commands.name: CreateDetails
Navigator Commands.description: Creates independent Detail databases.

Navigator Commands.name: CreateDrawings
Navigator Commands.description: Creates Drawing elements on the specified or active layout from navigator items.

Navigator Commands.name: CreateInteriorElevations
Navigator Commands.description: Creates Interior Elevation elements on the floor plan. Every consecutive pair of the given points becomes one segment, each with its own viewpoint - feed it the corner points of a room to get an interior elevation of that room.

Navigator Commands.name: CreateLayout
Navigator Commands.description: Creates Layouts and their backing master layouts. Archicad inserts a new layout at the first place of its subset, renumbering the sheets after it; previousNavigatorItemId or position 'last' places it after an existing sheet or at the end instead.

Navigator Commands.name: CreateLayoutSubset
Navigator Commands.description: Creates Layout Book subsets.

Navigator Commands.name: CreateSections
Navigator Commands.description: Creates Section elements on the floor plan.

Navigator Commands.name: CreateViewMapFolder
Navigator Commands.description: Creates a new folder in the View Map.

Navigator Commands.name: CreateViewsInViewMap
Navigator Commands.description: Creates independent (non-clone) navigator views in a specified View Map folder, by copying database and settings from source items.

Navigator Commands.name: CreateWorksheets
Navigator Commands.description: Creates independent Worksheet databases.

Navigator Commands.name: DeleteNavigatorItems
Navigator Commands.description: Deletes navigator items from the navigator tree: views and folders of the View Map, layouts and master layouts of the Layout Book, and independent worksheets and details of the Project Map. Layout subsets and marker-linked worksheets and details cannot be deleted.

Navigator Commands.name: FitInWindow
Navigator Commands.description: Zooms to the given elements or fits everything in the window.

Navigator Commands.name: Get3DCutPlanes
Navigator Commands.description: Gets whether the 3D cut planes are on and the cut planes (pa, pb, pc, pd) of the 3D window, in the form accepted by Set3DCutPlanes.

Navigator Commands.name: Get3DProjectionSettings
Navigator Commands.description: Gets the 3D projection settings of the 3D window: whether it is perspective or axonometric, the camera and target position, view cone, roll angle, distance and azimuth of a perspective, or the transformation matrix of an axonometry.

Navigator Commands.name: Get3DStyleDetails
Navigator Commands.description: Gets the settings of 3D styles by name (an empty name or no names means the current 3D style): rendering engine, model type, monochrome and background colors, contours, shadows and hatching. Available from Archicad 27.

Navigator Commands.name: Get3DWindowSettings
Navigator Commands.description: Gets the 3D window settings: the pixel size of the 3D window and the zoom (scale and displacement) of its projection.

Navigator Commands.name: GetActiveGraphicalOverrideCombination
Navigator Commands.description: Gets the graphic override combination applied to the current window, with its id and name. The response is empty when no combination is applied. This is the combination of the window itself, not the one stored in a saved view (see GetViewSettings). Available from Archicad 30.

Navigator Commands.name: GetDatabaseIdFromNavigatorItemId
Navigator Commands.description: Gets the ID of the database associated with the supplied navigator item id

Navigator Commands.name: GetDatabases
Navigator Commands.description: Lists every database of the given types (sections, elevations, interior elevations, details, worksheets, 3D documents, layouts, master layouts) with its database ID, name and reference ID, without walking the navigator trees.

Navigator Commands.name: GetDrawingContentBoxes
Navigator Commands.description: Returns the full content box of the given Drawing elements, independent of their frames, as ACAPI_Drawing_GetFullDrawingContentBox reports it. Available from Archicad 27.

Navigator Commands.name: GetLayoutCustomScheme
Navigator Commands.description: Gets the Layout Info Panel custom field definitions (name and key) from Book Settings.

Navigator Commands.name: GetLayoutSettings
Navigator Commands.description: Gets settings of layouts, including their master layout and Layout Info Panel custom data fields.

Navigator Commands.name: GetLayoutSubsetSettings
Navigator Commands.description: Gets the settings of existing Layout Book subsets: the same fields CreateLayoutSubset accepts (name, ID prefix, numbering style, ...).

Navigator Commands.name: GetModelViewOptions
Navigator Commands.description: Gets all model view options

Navigator Commands.name: GetNavigatorItemTree
Navigator Commands.description: Returns the full navigator item tree for the specified map. With includeChildCount true every item also reports the number of its direct children.

Navigator Commands.name: GetNavigatorParentItems
Navigator Commands.description: Returns the parent of each given navigator item: the folder, subset or layout book item it is in. The root of a map has no parent and gets an error.

Navigator Commands.name: GetStructureDisplay
Navigator Commands.description: Gets the Partial Structure Display (EntireStructure, CoreOnly, WithoutFinishes or StructureOnly) of the current window, and whether it is the 3D window. This is the setting of the window itself, not the one stored in a saved view (see GetViewSettings). Available from Archicad 27.

Navigator Commands.name: GetView2DTransformations
Navigator Commands.description: Get zoom and rotation of 2D views

Navigator Commands.name: GetViewSettings
Navigator Commands.description: Gets the view settings of navigator items

Navigator Commands.name: MoveNavigatorItem
Navigator Commands.description: Moves a navigator item to a new parent in the navigator tree.

Navigator Commands.name: PublishPublisherSet
Navigator Commands.description: Performs a publish operation on the currently opened project. Only the given publisher set will be published.

Navigator Commands.name: RenameNavigatorItem
Navigator Commands.description: Renames a navigator item or changes its ID. newId sets the custom layout number of a layout and the custom ID of any other item. Fails when Archicad refuses the change or does not apply the new name or ID (e.g. Project Map items, whose schedule items are named by their scheme). With customName false the item drops its custom name and follows its Project Map source again.

Navigator Commands.name: ResetZoom
Navigator Commands.description: Steps back in the zoom history of the current window, like Archicad's Zoom Back.

Navigator Commands.name: Set3DCutPlanes
Navigator Commands.description: Sets the 3D cut planes. An empty cutPlanes array switches the 3D cut off.

Navigator Commands.name: Set3DProjectionSettings
Navigator Commands.description: Sets a perspective projection for the 3D window. Every perspective parameter is required: read a known good set with Get3DProjectionSettings and pass it back, with the values to change replaced.

Navigator Commands.name: Set3DWindowSettings
Navigator Commands.description: Changes the pixel size of the 3D window and/or the zoom (scale and displacement) of its projection; the values not given are kept. Returns the settings read back after the change. Archicad may need a rebuild of the 3D window (RebuildView) before it shows the change, e.g. before SaveCurrentWindowAsImage.

Navigator Commands.name: SetActiveGraphicalOverrideCombination
Navigator Commands.description: Applies a graphic override combination, given by id or by name, to the current window. The current window must be a model window (floor plan, section, elevation, 3D, ...). To remove the overrides, apply the project's 'No Overrides' combination. The saved view is not changed (see SetViewSettings for that). Available from Archicad 30.

Navigator Commands.name: SetLayoutSettings
Navigator Commands.description: Sets settings of layouts, including their master layout and Layout Info Panel custom data fields.

Navigator Commands.name: SetStructureDisplay
Navigator Commands.description: Sets the Partial Structure Display (EntireStructure, CoreOnly, WithoutFinishes or StructureOnly) of the current window, e.g. the floor plan, a section or the 3D window. The change cannot be undone. The saved view is not changed (see SetViewSettings for that). Available from Archicad 27.

Navigator Commands.name: SetViewRotation
Navigator Commands.description: Set the rotation angle of 2D views via their floor plan database.

Navigator Commands.name: SetViewSettings
Navigator Commands.description: Sets the view settings of navigator items

Navigator Commands.name: SetZoom
Navigator Commands.description: Zooms the current 2D window to the given box in model coordinates.

Navigator Commands.name: UpdateDrawings
Navigator Commands.description: Performs a drawing update on the given elements.

Project Commands.name: ChangeHotlinkInstances
Project Commands.description: Moves, rotates or mirrors placed hotlink instances by changing their transformation. MoveElements and RotateElements do not work on hotlink instances.

Project Commands.name: ChangeHotlinkNodes
Project Commands.description: Repoints hotlink module nodes at other source files, as the Hotlink Manager's Relink button does. Follow it with UpdateHotlinks to re-read the content.

Project Commands.name: CloseProject
Project Commands.description: Closes the currently opened project.

Project Commands.name: CreateHotlinkInstances
Project Commands.description: Places instances of hotlink module nodes at an origin, rotation and mirroring.

Project Commands.name: CreateHotlinkNodes
Project Commands.description: Creates hotlink module nodes from source files. A node that already points at the same file is returned instead of duplicated (Archicad 26 and later; 25 cannot see an unplaced node).

Project Commands.name: CreateProjectInfoFields
Project Commands.description: Creates one or more custom project info fields.

Project Commands.name: DeleteProjectInfoFields
Project Commands.description: Deletes one or more custom project info fields. Hardcoded fields cannot be deleted.

Project Commands.name: GetAutoTextKeys
Project Commands.description: Retrieves the available autotext keys (name and embeddable key), optionally for a specific element. Embed a key in a Text or Label content by surrounding it with '<' and '>'.

Project Commands.name: GetAutoTextName
Project Commands.description: Retrieves the display names of one or more autotext keys (as returned inside a '<...>' embedded key), with a direct guid lookup for property-based keys instead of enumerating every property definition.

Project Commands.name: GetCalculationUnits
Project Commands.description: Gets the project calculation units.

Project Commands.name: GetCurrentViewImage
Project Commands.description: Returns what the 3D window, or the PhotoRendering window, shows as a base64 encoded png or jpg image with its size in pixels, without writing a file. Available from Archicad 30.

Project Commands.name: GetGeoLocation
Project Commands.description: Gets the project location details: the project location, and the survey point's position, geo-referencing parameters, visibility and lock state (the lock from Archicad 26).

Project Commands.name: GetHotlinkProxyElementTable
Project Commands.description: Maps the proxy elements of placed hotlink instances to the elements of the source file they were made from, so an element seen in a hotlinked module can be traced back to its source element.

Project Commands.name: GetHotlinks
Project Commands.description: Gets the file system locations (path) of the hotlink modules and the instance elements placed from each node. The hotlinks can have tree hierarchy in the project.

Project Commands.name: GetNoteAutoTextKeywords
Project Commands.description: Retrieves the keywords of note autotexts (the autotexts of dimension, label and other element notes) by their numeric API_NoteAutotextID values. Available from Archicad 26.

Project Commands.name: GetProjectInfo
Project Commands.description: Retrieves information about the currently loaded project.

Project Commands.name: GetProjectInfoFields
Project Commands.description: Retrieves the names and values of all project info fields.

Project Commands.name: GetProjectNotes
Project Commands.description: Gets the Project Notes of the project (File > Info > Project Notes): client, project name, company, address, architect, draftsmen, project status, date of issue, keywords and notes.

Project Commands.name: GetProjectPreferences
Project Commands.description: Gets pages of the project preferences (Options > Project Preferences): the working units, the dimensions and the calculation units. Further pages may follow.

Project Commands.name: GetStories
Project Commands.description: Retrieves information about the story structure of the currently loaded project: index, floor id, name, level, height and, from Archicad 28, the IFC GlobalId of each story.

Project Commands.name: GetSurveyPointTransformation
Project Commands.description: Gets the 3x4 matrix that transforms points from the Project Origin coordinate system into the Survey Point coordinate system, row by row, and its inverse when it is invertible. Read only. Available from Archicad 27.

Project Commands.name: NewProject
Project Commands.description: Starts a new, untitled project from the template set in Archicad's New Project settings, as File > New does; with newAndReset also the working environment is reset, as New and Reset All does. The unsaved changes of the open project are discarded, as with OpenProject.

Project Commands.name: OpenProject
Project Commands.description: Opens the given project.

Project Commands.name: PrintView
Project Commands.description: Prints from the current view.

Project Commands.name: RebuildView
Project Commands.description: Rebuilds the current view.

Project Commands.name: SaveAsModuleFile
Project Commands.description: Saves the given elements, or the current selection, as a hotlink module (.mod) file.

Project Commands.name: SaveCurrentWindowAsImage
Project Commands.description: Saves what the current window shows as an image file (png, jpg, bmp, tiff or gif), as File > Save as does with a picture format.

Project Commands.name: SaveProject
Project Commands.description: Saves the currently opened project.

Project Commands.name: SaveProjectAsArchive
Project Commands.description: Saves the open project as an archive (.pla) file, with the library parts it uses inside.

Project Commands.name: SetGeoLocation
Project Commands.description: Sets the project location details: the project location, and the survey point's position, geo-referencing parameters, visibility and lock state (the lock from Archicad 26). Omitted fields stay unchanged.

Project Commands.name: SetProjectInfoField
Project Commands.description: Sets the value of a project info field.

Project Commands.name: SetProjectNotes
Project Commands.description: Changes the Project Notes of the project (File > Info > Project Notes). Only the given fields are changed; texts longer than the field Archicad stores are truncated.

Project Commands.name: SetProjectPreferences
Project Commands.description: Changes pages of the project preferences (Options > Project Preferences): the working units, the dimensions and the calculation units. Only the given fields change, the rest of each page keeps its value. In Teamwork the PreferencesDialog lockable object set has to be reserved first (ReserveLockableObjectSet). Available from Archicad 27.

Project Commands.name: SetStories
Project Commands.description: Sets the story sructure of the currently loaded project.

Project Commands.name: UpdateHotlinks
Project Commands.description: Re-reads the source files of hotlink module nodes and refreshes their cached content in the project, as the Hotlink Manager's Update button does.

Element Commands.name: ChangeSelectionOfElements
Element Commands.description: Adds/removes a number of elements to/from the current selection.

Element Commands.name: ConvertRevealOffsets
Element Commands.description: Converts the reveal depth offset of windows and doors placed in walls between the two references Archicad uses: measured from the core skin of a composite wall, or from the wall side. Give exactly one of coreOffset or sideOffset per opening; both values are returned. For walls with a basic structure the two values are equal. The output is aligned with the input array of openings. Available from Archicad 27.

Element Commands.name: DeleteElements
Element Commands.description: Deletes elements. The zones of the call are deleted before all the other elements, so an automatic zone deleted together with its bounding walls is gone before its boundary is; deleting the boundary of an automatic zone without the zone itself can open Archicad's modal 'No closed polygon found' dialog, which blocks the command until someone clicks it in Archicad. Returns an execution result for each input element: an element that could not be deleted (for example because its layer is locked) gets a failed execution result instead of being skipped silently.

Element Commands.name: DeleteSelectedElements
Element Commands.description: Deletes the currently selected elements in one undo step, the same as pressing the Delete key.

Element Commands.name: FilterElements
Element Commands.description: Keeps the elements that match all the given criteria: Archicad's flag filters (filters), layer (layerIndices), home story (floorIndices) and element type (elementTypes). Within one criterion any of the listed values matches; an omitted criterion does not filter.

Element Commands.name: Get3DBoundingBoxes
Element Commands.description: Get the 3D bounding box of elements. The bounding box is calculated from the global origin in the 3D view. The output is the array of the bounding boxes respective to the input array of elements.

Element Commands.name: Get3DGeometryOfElements
Element Commands.description: Gets the 3D geometry of elements as the solid bodies of their 3D model: a vertex list in world coordinates and the planar faces (with their holes) referencing it, each face with its surface attribute when that is a project attribute. The bodies of the subelements of a Stair, Railing or Curtain Wall, and of the segments of a Column or Beam, are included. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. The 3D model of the elements is generated as needed, so many elements can take a while.

Element Commands.name: GetAllElements
Element Commands.description: Returns the identifier of all elements on the plan. Use the optional filter parameter for filtering. Objects that belong to another element (zone stamps, the parts of stairs and railings) are left out unless the IncludeSubElemObjects filter is given.

Element Commands.name: GetCategoryValuesOfElements
Element Commands.description: Gets the category values (Structural Function, Position, Renovation Status ...) of the given elements, optionally only for the given category types. An element that has none of the requested categories (an annotation, for example) gets an error item. The names are localized: use the type and the categoryValueId in scripts.

Element Commands.name: GetCollisions
Element Commands.description: Detect collisions between the given two groups of elements.

Element Commands.name: GetConnectedElements
Element Commands.description: Gets the elements hosted by (connected to) the given owner elements, filtered to the given element type: for example the Windows or Doors of a Wall, the frames, panels, junctions and accessories of a Curtain Wall, the risers, treads and structures of a Stair, or the posts, rails and panels of a Railing.

Element Commands.name: GetDetailsOfElements
Element Commands.description: Gets the details of the given elements (geometry parameters etc). Use the optional fields parameter to return only the fields you need and skip the computation of the others (for example floorPlanPolygons).

Element Commands.name: GetDimensionData
Element Commands.description: Gets witness point data (coordinates, measured values) from existing dimension chains.

Element Commands.name: GetElementAtCoordinate
Element Commands.description: Finds the element of the given polygonal type (for example Slab, Roof, Mesh, Zone or Hatch) at a coordinate of the floor plan of the current database, the way a click there would. Use the optional filters parameter (the values of FilterElements) to consider only, for example, the elements visible by layer, and the optional z parameter to give the elevation of the point. Returns found: false when there is no such element. Useful together with GetPointFromUser.

Element Commands.name: GetElementCategories
Element Commands.description: Lists the element categories of the project (Structural Function, Position, Renovation Status, Renovation Filter and, in the German version, BRI) with their possible values. The names of the categories and values are localized: identify a category by its type and a value by its categoryValueId, never by name.

Element Commands.name: GetElementPreviewImage
Element Commands.description: Returns the preview image of the given element.

Element Commands.name: GetElementTypeNames
Element Commands.description: Gets the localized names of the given element types, as the running Archicad shows them (for example 'Wand' for Wall in German Archicad). The output is aligned with the input array of element types. Available from Archicad 27.

Element Commands.name: GetElementsByType
Element Commands.description: Returns the identifier of every element of the given type on the plan. It works for any type. Use the optional filter parameter for filtering. Objects that belong to another element (zone stamps, the parts of stairs and railings) are left out unless the IncludeSubElemObjects filter is given.

Element Commands.name: GetElementsInDrawOrder
Element Commands.description: Returns the identifier of every element of the current database, or of the given databases, in Archicad's drawing order (the order set by Bring to Front and Send to Back), as ACAPI_DrawOrder_DrawOrderGetNext walks it. Use the optional elementType and filters parameters for filtering. Objects that belong to another element (zone stamps, the parts of stairs and railings) are left out unless the IncludeSubElemObjects filter is given.

Element Commands.name: GetGDLParametersOfElements
Element Commands.description: Gets all the GDL parameters (name, type, value) of the given elements.

Element Commands.name: GetGridElementDefaults
Element Commands.description: Returns the Grid Tool defaults: library part, size and GDL parameters of a new grid element. Needs Archicad 26 or later.

Element Commands.name: GetGridElements
Element Commands.description: Lists the grid elements (placed with the Grid Tool or created by CreateGridElements) with their position, angle, size, library part and optionally GDL parameters. Needs Archicad 26 or later.

Element Commands.name: GetHierarchicalElementOwners
Element Commands.description: Gets the owner of each given element in its hierarchical element: the root (e.g. the Curtain Wall, Stair or Railing of a frame, tread or post) or the immediate parent. Also returns whether the given element is a main element, a subelement or not part of a hierarchical element.

Element Commands.name: GetLinksOfElements
Element Commands.description: Gets the links created by LinkElements that start from the given elements: the linked element and the flags of each link. Links pointing to an element are not returned; query the elements they start from. Returns an error item for an element that does not exist.

Element Commands.name: GetMarkerParametersOfElements
Element Commands.description: Gets the marker library part and the marker's GDL parameters (name, type, value) of the given Window and Door elements. The marker is the stamp drawn next to the opening on the floor plan; its parameters are separate from the opening's own GDL parameters, which GetGDLParametersOfElements returns.

Element Commands.name: GetOpeningDefault
Element Commands.description: Returns the settings of the Opening tool defaults: the extrusion parameters (as GetOpeningDetails returns them) and the floor plan parameters (as GetOpeningFloorPlanParameters returns them). Available from Archicad 29.

Element Commands.name: GetOpeningDetails
Element Commands.description: Returns the details of Opening elements: the parent element, the cut and connected elements, the geometry (anchor point, extrusion direction, axes, polygon) and the extrusion parameters (size, anchor, offsets, surface overrides). Available from Archicad 29.

Element Commands.name: GetOpeningFloorPlanParameters
Element Commands.description: Returns the floor plan parameters of Opening elements: the reference axis, the cut surface and outline lines, the cover fills and the cut and uncut symbols. Available from Archicad 29.

Element Commands.name: GetOpeningTransformations
Element Commands.description: Gets the placement of Opening elements without changing them: the global-to-local transformation matrix Archicad returns, its inverse, and the origin and axes of the opening in world coordinates derived from the inverse. Mirrored openings give a left-handed matrix (isMirrored). Needs Archicad 27 or later.

Element Commands.name: GetQuantitiesOfElements
Element Commands.description: Gets the quantities of the given elements calculated by Archicad (volumes, surfaces, lengths etc.), together with the volume and projected area per building material (one item per skin of composite and complex profile elements, one item for basic elements). Supported types: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Zone, ColumnSegment, BeamSegment. Use the optional minOpeningSize parameter to control the conditional values, and calculateInOneCall to calculate all the elements in one Archicad call.

Element Commands.name: GetRelationsOfElements
Element Commands.description: Gets the type-specific relations of the given elements: endpoint and reference line connections of walls, beams and beam segments, boundary elements and boundary sections of zones, the zones on the two sides of windows, doors, skylights and curtain wall panels, and the zones connected to roofs and shells. Available from Archicad 26.

Element Commands.name: GetRoomImage
Element Commands.description: Returns the room image of the given zone.

Element Commands.name: GetSectionElements
Element Commands.description: Gets the elements drawn in the given section, elevation or interior elevation databases, each with the owner element it was generated from. This is the only command that returns raw section element identifiers - every other listing command converts them to their owner - so it is the way to obtain the sectionElementId that CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection requires.

Element Commands.name: GetSelectedElements
Element Commands.description: Gets the list of the currently selected elements.

Element Commands.name: GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements
Element Commands.description: Gets the subelements of the given hierarchical elements. From Archicad 28 the subelements of external hierarchical elements (for example MEP elements or elements of other add-ons) are returned as externalSubelements.

Element Commands.name: GetSurfaceQuantitiesOfElements
Element Commands.description: Gets the exposed surface areas of the given elements calculated by Archicad: for each element one item per surface attribute and building material pair with the area that is not covered by the covering elements (for example the wall area behind a slab is taken off the wall's surface). The covering elements are the optional coverElements; by default every construction element of the project. The output is aligned with the input array of elements.

Element Commands.name: GetZoneBoundaries
Element Commands.description: Gets the boundaries of the given Zones (connected elements, neighbour zones, etc.). Accepts either a single zoneElementId or a list of zones. Prefer the list: the expensive boundary recalculation runs once per call, so querying many Zones in one call is much faster than calling the command once per Zone.

Element Commands.name: GetZoneReductions
Element Commands.description: Gets the area reductions of the given Zones, as the Zone Stamp's area calculation uses them: the polygons of the Zone covered by Walls, Columns, reducing Fills, sloping Roofs and low ceilings, each with its type, the percentage it is reduced by, its area and its outline with holes. Area calculations by local standards need these parts, which GetQuantitiesOfElements only gives as totals. The output is aligned with the input array of elements.

Element Commands.name: HighlightElements
Element Commands.description: Highlights the elements given in the elements array. In case of empty elements array removes all previously set highlights.

Element Commands.name: LinkElements
Element Commands.description: Creates persistent links between pairs of elements, each from one element to another, with an optional integer flags value per link. Scripts can record their own relations between elements this way (for example which label documents which column) instead of storing GUIDs in properties. The links are stored in the project and have no effect on geometry; they are independent from groups, hotlinks and solid element operations. A link is directional: it is returned by GetLinksOfElements for the element it starts from only, and removed by UnlinkElements. Undoable.

Element Commands.name: LockElements
Element Commands.description: Locks the given elements. Manual lock, not teamwork!

Element Commands.name: MeasureTexts
Element Commands.description: Measures texts before placing them: the length of every line for a given font, style and height, on paper in millimetres or in the model at the current drawing scale, and the font's capital size factor. Creates nothing.

Element Commands.name: MirrorElements
Element Commands.description: Mirrors elements across an axis given by two points on the floor plan, optionally as a copy. An element that cannot be edited (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not available in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason instead of being skipped silently.

Element Commands.name: MoveElements
Element Commands.description: Moves elements with a given vector. An element that cannot be edited (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not available in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason instead of being skipped silently.

Element Commands.name: RegularizePolygons
Element Commands.description: Regularizes polygons with Archicad's own polygon regularization, before they are used to create slabs, zones or fills: removes duplicate points, fixes the orientation, resolves self-intersections and touching holes. Each input polygon gives 0, 1 or more valid polygons in the format of CreateSlabs, optionally with the input vertex and edge each result vertex and edge came from. Changes nothing in the project.

Element Commands.name: RegularizePolylines
Element Commands.description: Regularizes polylines with Archicad's own polyline regularization: removes repeated consecutive points. The result is in the format of CreatePolylines and may be empty, optionally with the input point and segment each result point and segment came from. Changes nothing in the project.

Element Commands.name: RemoveElementNotificationClient
Element Commands.description: Removes an element notification client.

Element Commands.name: RotateElements
Element Commands.description: Rotates elements around a reference point. An element that cannot be edited (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not available in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason instead of being skipped silently.

Element Commands.name: RunParameterScriptOfElements
Element Commands.description: Runs the parameter script of the library part of the given elements (objects, lamps, windows, doors, etc.), so that parameter values that depend on other parameters are updated, e.g. after SetGDLParametersOfElements.

Element Commands.name: SetCategoryValuesOfElements
Element Commands.description: Sets the category values (Structural Function, Position, Renovation Status ...) of the given elements, one element and one category per item, in a single undoable step. The value must belong to the given category, as GetElementCategories lists them; an element without that category gets a failed execution result. The names are localized: use the type and the categoryValueId in scripts.

Element Commands.name: SetDetailsOfElements
Element Commands.description: Sets the details of the given elements (floor, layer, order, Element ID etc).

Element Commands.name: SetElementNotificationClient
Element Commands.description: Sets up a new notification client to receive element events.

Element Commands.name: SetGDLParametersOfElements
Element Commands.description: Sets the given GDL parameters of the given elements. An element Archicad does not let the user edit (its layer locked, the element locked, or not reserved by the user in Teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming that reason, whatever the parameter.

Element Commands.name: SetMarkerParametersOfElements
Element Commands.description: Sets the given GDL parameters of the marker of the given Window and Door elements. The opening's own settings and the other marker parameters are left as they are.

Element Commands.name: SetOpeningDetails
Element Commands.description: Changes the details of Opening elements: the parent element, the cut elements, the polygon, a transformation of the geometry and the extrusion parameters (size, anchor, offsets, surface overrides) returned by GetOpeningDetails. Available from Archicad 29.

Element Commands.name: SetOpeningFloorPlanParameters
Element Commands.description: Changes the floor plan parameters of Opening elements returned by GetOpeningFloorPlanParameters, and sets or removes their cut and uncut symbols. Available from Archicad 29.

Element Commands.name: SetZoneLabelingSettings
Element Commands.description: Turns the automatic labeling of Zones on or off. Available from Archicad 28.

Element Commands.name: SolveStairBaseline
Element Commands.description: Runs the Archicad stair solver on the given Stair baselines and parameters without creating any element. Returns for each one whether the baseline was already correct, could be solved or could not be solved, with the baseline and the main stair settings after solving. Available from Archicad 27.

Element Commands.name: TriangulatePolygonsOfElements
Element Commands.description: Triangulates the plan polygon of the given elements, holes excluded, as Archicad does it: the outline of a Slab, Zone, Hatch or Mesh and the polygon of a Roof. Each triangle is given by the 2D coordinates of its three vertices. The output is aligned with the input array of elements; an element of another type gets an error item.

Element Commands.name: UnlinkElements
Element Commands.description: Removes the links created by LinkElements between the given pairs of elements. The direction matters: the link starting from fromElementId and pointing to toElementId is removed. Undoable.

Element Commands.name: UnlockElements
Element Commands.description: Unlocks the given elements. Manual lock, not teamwork!

Element Commands.name: UpdateZones
Element Commands.description: Updates all Zones (recalculates their geometry, updates their Zone Stamps and the connected elements).

Application Commands.name: ChangeWindow
Application Commands.description: Changes the current (active) window to the given window. A databaseId on its own is enough; the window type is taken from the database. With windowType 'FloorPlan' and a storyIndex it also activates that story on the floor plan.

Application Commands.name: Get3DCutawayStatus
Application Commands.description: Returns whether 3D Cutaway is on and whether the cutting planes are shown in the 3D window. In Archicad 25-27 the 3D window may need to be open.

Application Commands.name: GetAddOnVersion
Application Commands.description: Retrieves the version of the Tapir Additional JSON Commands Add-On.

Application Commands.name: GetArchicadLocation
Application Commands.description: Retrieves the location of the currently running Archicad executable.

Application Commands.name: GetArchicadReleaseInfo
Application Commands.description: Retrieves the main version, release version and build number of the running Archicad, with the caption of its window.

Application Commands.name: GetContainingDatabases
Application Commands.description: Returns the database (window type, database id and name) that contains each of the given elements, from any database, not only the current one. Pass the windowType and databaseId to ChangeWindow to open it, for example to find an element placed on a layout.

Application Commands.name: GetCurrentWindowDrawingScale
Application Commands.description: Returns the drawing scale of the current (active) window, the scale shown in the bottom bar, as its denominator: 100.0 for 1:100, 20.0 for 1:20. Unlike GetViewSettings it needs no saved view. It reads the scale of the current database: the floor plan, a section, elevation, interior elevation, detail, worksheet or 3D document window, each of which has its own. Layouts always return 1.0.

Application Commands.name: GetCurrentWindowType
Application Commands.description: Returns the type of the current (active) window.

Application Commands.name: GetElementFromUser
Application Commands.description: Asks the designer to click an element in the current window and returns its id, its type and the clicked point. A click on empty space or on an element of a type not asked for asks again. Archicad waits for the click or for Escape, and every other JSON command queues behind this one until then; cancelling returns cancelled.

Application Commands.name: GetPointFromUser
Application Commands.description: Asks the designer to click a point in the current window and returns it. Archicad waits for the click or for Escape, and every other JSON command queues behind this one until then; the call fails when the input is cancelled.

Application Commands.name: GetPrinterInfo
Application Commands.description: Retrieves Archicad's current print settings: the print area, grid, fixed text size and scale (the settings PrintView takes).

Application Commands.name: GetProductVersionInfo
Application Commands.description: Retrieves the version information of the running Archicad: build number, language code, product family and version text, plus the product name, product type and main/update/hotfix versions from Archicad 29. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

Application Commands.name: GetSpecialFolders
Application Commands.description: Retrieves the filesystem paths of the special folders of the running Archicad (preferences, cache, data, temporary, application, defaults, templates, help, embedded project library, etc.).

Application Commands.name: GetUserGSID
Application Commands.description: Get the current registered User-GSID and OrganizationsID. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

Application Commands.name: QuitArchicad
Application Commands.description: Performs a quit operation on the currently running Archicad instance.

Application Commands.name: Set3DCutawayStatus
Application Commands.description: Turns 3D Cutaway on or off and shows or hides the cutting planes in the 3D window. In Archicad 25-27 the 3D window may need to be open.

Application Commands.name: SetCurrentWindowDrawingScale
Application Commands.description: Changes the drawing scale of the current (active) window, the scale shown in the bottom bar, to the given denominator: 100 for 1:100. It changes the scale of the current database: the floor plan, a section, elevation, interior elevation, detail, worksheet or 3D document window, each of which has its own. Layouts are always 1:1 and are rejected. The scale must be between 1 and 30000. The change is undoable.

Application Commands.name: SetDialogAutoClose
Application Commands.description: Turns the dialog auto close on or off. While it is on, Archicad closes the dialogs it would show with their default button instead of waiting for the user, so automation is not blocked by them. To have it on already while Archicad opens a project (before any command can be sent), set the TAPIR_DIALOG_AUTOCLOSE environment variable to true for the Archicad process before starting it.

Application Commands.name: ShowAlert
Application Commands.description: Display a dialog with up to three buttons.

MEP Commands.name: ConnectMEPElements
MEP Commands.description: Connects MEP routing elements to other MEP elements or routes. Merges routes, splits routes or creates branch elements as needed. Available from Archicad 28.

MEP Commands.name: ConnectToElectricalCircuits
MEP Commands.description: Connects electrical devices, or panels as sub-panels, to electrical circuits. Available from Archicad 30.

MEP Commands.name: CreateElectricalCircuits
MEP Commands.description: Adds new circuits to electrical panels, optionally with the given description, voltage, wiring type and used phases. Available from Archicad 30.

MEP Commands.name: CreateElectricalDevices
MEP Commands.description: Places electrical devices with the default settings of the Electrical Device tool, optionally with the given library part, size, rotation, mirroring, apparent power and load classification, and connects them to a circuit. Available from Archicad 30.

MEP Commands.name: CreateElectricalPanels
MEP Commands.description: Places electrical panels with the default settings of the Electrical Panel tool, optionally with the given library part, size, rotation, mirroring, panel name and circuit naming. Available from Archicad 30.

MEP Commands.name: CreateMEPElements
MEP Commands.description: Creates MEP elements (Terminal, Accessory, Equipment or Fitting) at the given positions. Available from Archicad 28.

MEP Commands.name: CreateMEPPhysicalSystems
MEP Commands.description: Creates physical systems in MEP system groups, optionally with a root element and an MEP system as their category. Available from Archicad 29.

MEP Commands.name: CreateMEPRoutingElements
MEP Commands.description: Creates MEP routing elements (duct, pipe or cable carrier routes) along the given polylines with optional cross section data (shape, size, preference table and reference id), MEP system and layer (also set on the segments, elbows and transitions). Available from Archicad 28.

MEP Commands.name: CreateMEPSystemGroups
MEP Commands.description: Creates MEP system groups. Available from Archicad 29.

MEP Commands.name: DeleteElectricalCircuits
MEP Commands.description: Removes electrical circuits from their panels. Available from Archicad 30.

MEP Commands.name: DeleteMEPPhysicalSystems
MEP Commands.description: Removes MEP physical systems from their system groups. Their member elements are not deleted. Available from Archicad 29.

MEP Commands.name: GetElectricalCircuits
MEP Commands.description: Gets the given electrical circuits, the circuits of the given panels, or every circuit of the project: name, description, owner panel, connected devices and panels, voltage, phases, wiring type, loads, voltage drop and estimated cable length. Available from Archicad 30.

MEP Commands.name: GetElectricalDevices
MEP Commands.description: Gets the electrical devices (lights, sockets and other consumers) of the project or the given ones: parent circuit, placement, apparent power, load classification, demand load and directly connected MEP elements. Available from Archicad 30.

MEP Commands.name: GetElectricalPanels
MEP Commands.description: Gets the electrical panels (distribution boards) of the project or the given ones: name, circuit naming, circuits, parent circuit, placement and the connected and demand loads in total and per phase. Available from Archicad 30.

MEP Commands.name: GetElectricalProjectSettings
MEP Commands.description: Gets the electrical project settings: the default voltage, the wiring types with their cross-sectional area and the load classifications with their demand factor. Available from Archicad 30.

MEP Commands.name: GetMEPDistributionSystems
MEP Commands.description: Retrieves the MEP distribution systems of the project with their domain, MEP system attribute and member elements. Available from Archicad 28.

MEP Commands.name: GetMEPElements
MEP Commands.description: Retrieves the MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing) elements of the project, optionally filtered by type and domain. MEP elements are ordinary elements, so the generic element commands work on them as well (for example they can be deleted with the DeleteElements command). Available from Archicad 28.

MEP Commands.name: GetMEPPorts
MEP Commands.description: Retrieves the ports of the given MEP elements including position, shape, size and connection status. Available from Archicad 28.

MEP Commands.name: GetMEPPreferenceTables
MEP Commands.description: Gets the circular cross section preference tables (referenceId, diameter, description) and the reference set of the Piping or Ventilation domain, optionally with the elbow, branch and transition preference tables. The angle set and the transition tables are available from Archicad 29. Available from Archicad 28.

MEP Commands.name: GetMEPRoutingElements
MEP Commands.description: Retrieves the details of the given MEP routing elements: domain, MEP system, offset from the home story, branch preference table, the ports logically connected at the route's beginning and end, route polyline, segments with cross section data (shape, size, preference table and reference id), begin and end nodes, anchor, reference line offsets, wall thickness, flange size and rigid segments, and nodes with their incoming and outgoing segments, elbows and transitions. Available from Archicad 28.

MEP Commands.name: GetMEPSystemGroups
MEP Commands.description: Gets the MEP system groups of the project with their physical systems: name, editable flag, root element and MEP system. Available from Archicad 29.

MEP Commands.name: ModifyElectricalCircuits
MEP Commands.description: Modifies the description, voltage, wiring type and used phases of electrical circuits. Available from Archicad 30.

MEP Commands.name: ModifyElectricalDevices
MEP Commands.description: Modifies the apparent power, load classification and placement (anchor point, orientation, rotation, mirroring, library part, size) of electrical devices. Available from Archicad 30.

MEP Commands.name: ModifyElectricalPanels
MEP Commands.description: Modifies the name, circuit naming and placement (anchor point, orientation, rotation, mirroring, library part, size) of electrical panels. Available from Archicad 30.

MEP Commands.name: ModifyElectricalProjectSettings
MEP Commands.description: Modifies the electrical project settings: sets the default voltage and adds or removes wiring types and load classifications. Available from Archicad 30.

MEP Commands.name: ModifyMEPPhysicalSystems
MEP Commands.description: Modifies MEP physical systems: name, root element and the MEP system used as their category. Only the given fields are changed. Available from Archicad 29.

MEP Commands.name: ModifyMEPRoutingElements
MEP Commands.description: Modifies the given MEP routing elements: MEP system, branch preference table, cross section data (shape, size, preference table and reference id), anchor, reference line offsets, wall thickness and flange size of all segments, and node positions. Available from Archicad 28.

MEP Commands.name: ModifyMEPSystemGroups
MEP Commands.description: Renames MEP system groups. Available from Archicad 29.

Element Creation Commands.name: CreateArcs
Element Creation Commands.description: Creates Arc elements based on the given parameters.

Element Creation Commands.name: CreateAssociativeDimensions
Element Creation Commands.description: Creates associative linear dimensions from explicit witness point references. A witness point can also be static, given by its coordinate instead of an element.

Element Creation Commands.name: CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection
Element Creation Commands.description: Creates associative linear dimensions on section elements using common wall, slab, beam, column and opening presets. The preset points of multiple section elements can be merged into one continuous dimension chain via sectionElementIds.

Element Creation Commands.name: CreateBeams
Element Creation Commands.description: Creates Beam elements based on the given parameters.

Element Creation Commands.name: CreateCircles
Element Creation Commands.description: Creates Circle elements based on the given parameters.

Element Creation Commands.name: CreateColumns
Element Creation Commands.description: Creates Column elements based on the given parameters.

Element Creation Commands.name: CreateCurtainWalls
Element Creation Commands.description: Creates Curtain Wall elements along a reference polyline with a column (primary) and row (secondary) pattern. The frame and panel classes come from the favorite or from the Curtain Wall tool defaults; the pattern cells can assign them to the grid.

Element Creation Commands.name: CreateDoors
Element Creation Commands.description: Creates Door elements in host walls based on the given parameters.

Element Creation Commands.name: CreateGridElements
Element Creation Commands.description: Creates grid elements, the elements the Grid Tool places, from begin and end coordinates, with optional story, layer and GDL parameters. Needs Archicad 26 or later.

Element Creation Commands.name: CreateHatches
Element Creation Commands.description: Creates Hatch elements based on the given parameters.

Element Creation Commands.name: CreateHotspots
Element Creation Commands.description: Creates Hotspot elements based on the given parameters.

Element Creation Commands.name: CreateLabels
Element Creation Commands.description: Creates Label elements based on the given parameters.

Element Creation Commands.name: CreateLamps
Element Creation Commands.description: Creates Lamp elements based on the given parameters.

Element Creation Commands.name: CreateLevelDimensions
Element Creation Commands.description: Creates Level Dimension elements (the Level Dimension tool) based on the given parameters. With a parentElementId the dimension is associative: it shows the height of the parent element (Mesh, Slab, Roof ...) at its position and follows the element when it changes.

Element Creation Commands.name: CreateLineElements
Element Creation Commands.description: Creates Line elements based on the given parameters.

Element Creation Commands.name: CreateMeshes
Element Creation Commands.description: Creates Mesh elements based on the given parameters.

Element Creation Commands.name: CreateMorphs
Element Creation Commands.description: Creates Morph elements from simple box definitions.

Element Creation Commands.name: CreateObjects
Element Creation Commands.description: Creates Object elements based on the given parameters.

Element Creation Commands.name: CreateOpenings
Element Creation Commands.description: Creates Opening elements in the given host elements.

Element Creation Commands.name: CreatePolylines
Element Creation Commands.description: Creates Polyline elements based on the given parameters.

Element Creation Commands.name: CreateRoofs
Element Creation Commands.description: Creates Roof elements based on footprint, level and roof profile data. Creates a multi-plane roof by default; pass 'pivotLine' (and optionally 'angle') to create a single-plane roof instead.

Element Creation Commands.name: CreateSlabs
Element Creation Commands.description: Creates Slab elements based on the given parameters.

Element Creation Commands.name: CreateSplines
Element Creation Commands.description: Creates Spline elements based on the given parameters.

Element Creation Commands.name: CreateStairs
Element Creation Commands.description: Creates Stair elements based on the given baseline and parameters.

Element Creation Commands.name: CreateTexts
Element Creation Commands.description: Creates standalone Text elements based on the given parameters.

Element Creation Commands.name: CreateWallThicknessDimensions
Element Creation Commands.description: Creates associative wall thickness dimensions for the given walls.

Element Creation Commands.name: CreateWalls
Element Creation Commands.description: Creates Wall elements based on the given parameters.

Element Creation Commands.name: CreateWindows
Element Creation Commands.description: Creates Window elements in host walls based on the given parameters.

Element Creation Commands.name: CreateZones
Element Creation Commands.description: Creates Zone elements based on the given parameters.

Attribute Commands.name: CreateAttributeFolders
Attribute Commands.description: Creates attribute folders, each given by attribute type and path (the folder names from the root folder down). Missing parent folders are created too; a folder that already exists is kept and reported as success. Available from Archicad 26.

Attribute Commands.name: CreateBuildingMaterials
Attribute Commands.description: Creates or overwrites Building Material attributes based on the given parameters.

Attribute Commands.name: CreateComposites
Attribute Commands.description: Creates or overwrites Composite attributes based on the given parameters.

Attribute Commands.name: CreateFills
Attribute Commands.description: Creates or overwrites Fill attributes based on the given parameters.

Attribute Commands.name: CreateGraphicOverrideCombinations
Attribute Commands.description: Creates graphic override combinations from existing rules. Available from Archicad 27.

Attribute Commands.name: CreateGraphicOverrideRules
Attribute Commands.description: Creates graphic override rules. The criterion is given as Archicad's criterion XML or as structured conditions. The rule group is created when no rule group has the given name. Available from Archicad 27.

Attribute Commands.name: CreateLayerCombinations
Attribute Commands.description: Creates or overwrites Layer Combination attributes based on the given parameters.

Attribute Commands.name: CreateLayers
Attribute Commands.description: Creates or overwrites Layer attributes based on the given parameters.

Attribute Commands.name: CreateLines
Attribute Commands.description: Creates or overwrites Line attributes based on the given parameters.

Attribute Commands.name: CreateMEPSystems
Attribute Commands.description: Creates or overwrites MEP System attributes (domain, pens, fill, center line type, surface and insulation surface) based on the given parameters.

Attribute Commands.name: CreatePenTables
Attribute Commands.description: Creates or overwrites Pen Table attributes based on the given parameters.

Attribute Commands.name: CreateProfiles
Attribute Commands.description: Creates or overwrites Profile attributes as a copy of an existing Profile's geometry, based on the given parameters.

Attribute Commands.name: CreateSurfaces
Attribute Commands.description: Creates or overwrites Surface attributes based on the given parameters.

Attribute Commands.name: CreateZoneCategories
Attribute Commands.description: Creates or overwrites Zone Category attributes based on the given parameters.

Attribute Commands.name: DeleteAttributeFolders
Attribute Commands.description: Deletes attribute folders, each given by attribute type and path, together with all the subfolders and deletable attributes they contain (a folder holding an attribute that cannot be deleted is kept). The root folder cannot be deleted. Available from Archicad 26.

Attribute Commands.name: DeleteAttributes
Attribute Commands.description: Deletes the given attributes.

Attribute Commands.name: DeleteGraphicOverrideCombinations
Attribute Commands.description: Deletes graphic override combinations. Their rules are kept. Available from Archicad 27.

Attribute Commands.name: DeleteGraphicOverrideRuleGroups
Attribute Commands.description: Deletes graphic override rule groups, found by name. A group that still contains rules is kept unless its rules are moved to another group or deleted with it. Available from Archicad 27.

Attribute Commands.name: DeleteGraphicOverrideRules
Attribute Commands.description: Deletes graphic override rules. They are also removed from the combinations that contain them. Available from Archicad 27.

Attribute Commands.name: GetAttributesByType
Attribute Commands.description: Returns the details of every attribute of the given type. From Archicad 30 an attribute that Archicad keeps a creation record of also carries creationInfo: how (method), from where (source), by whom and when it was created.

Attribute Commands.name: GetAttributesFromProject
Attribute Commands.description: Reads the attributes of the given types from another project or template file without opening it, for example to compare them with the attributes of the open project. Nothing is imported into the open project. The names are the legacy 8-bit names, so non-ASCII characters may not come through. Available from Archicad 27.

Attribute Commands.name: GetBuildingMaterialPhysicalProperties
Attribute Commands.description: Retrieves the physical properties of the given Building Materials.

Attribute Commands.name: GetBuildingMaterials
Attribute Commands.description: Returns the details of the given Building Material attributes.

Attribute Commands.name: GetComposites
Attribute Commands.description: Returns the details of the given Composite attributes.

Attribute Commands.name: GetCurrentLayerCombination
Attribute Commands.description: Returns the layer combination in effect in the current window. No layer combination is returned when the current state of the layers matches none.

Attribute Commands.name: GetCurrentPenTable
Attribute Commands.description: Returns the current Pen Table (its index, attribute identifier and name) and its number of pens. Pass the returned attributeId to GetPenTables to read the pens.

Attribute Commands.name: GetFills
Attribute Commands.description: Returns the details of the given Fill attributes.

Attribute Commands.name: GetFontsByName
Attribute Commands.description: Finds loaded fonts by name through Archicad's font search and returns their index (as Text and Label fields reference fonts in fontIndex) and name, or an error for a name no loaded font has.

Attribute Commands.name: GetGraphicOverrideCombinations
Attribute Commands.description: Gets all graphic override combinations of the project with the rules they contain. Available from Archicad 27.

Attribute Commands.name: GetGraphicOverrideRuleGroups
Attribute Commands.description: Gets all graphic override rule groups of the project with the rules they contain, empty groups included. Available from Archicad 27.

Attribute Commands.name: GetGraphicOverrideRules
Attribute Commands.description: Gets all graphic override rules of the project, with their rule group, criterion and style. Available from Archicad 27.

Attribute Commands.name: GetGraphicOverrideRulesByName
Attribute Commands.description: Gets graphic override rules by name, with their rule group, criterion and style. The rule group narrows the search; without it the rule is searched in every rule group. Available from Archicad 27.

Attribute Commands.name: GetLayerCombinations
Attribute Commands.description: Returns the details of layer combination attributes.

Attribute Commands.name: GetLayers
Attribute Commands.description: Returns the details of the given Layer attributes.

Attribute Commands.name: GetLines
Attribute Commands.description: Returns the details of the given Line attributes.

Attribute Commands.name: GetMEPSystems
Attribute Commands.description: Returns the details of the given MEP System attributes (domain, pens, fill, center line type, surface and insulation surface).

Attribute Commands.name: GetPenTables
Attribute Commands.description: Returns the details of the given Pen Table attributes.

Attribute Commands.name: GetProfiles
Attribute Commands.description: Returns the details of the given Profile attributes.

Attribute Commands.name: GetSurfaces
Attribute Commands.description: Returns the details of the given Surface attributes.

Attribute Commands.name: GetZoneCategories
Attribute Commands.description: Returns the details of the given Zone Category attributes.

Attribute Commands.name: ModifyGraphicOverrideRules
Attribute Commands.description: Modifies the name, criterion or style of graphic override rules. The criterion is given as Archicad's criterion XML or as structured conditions. A given style replaces the whole style of the rule. Available from Archicad 27.

Attribute Commands.name: MoveAttributesAndFolders
Attribute Commands.description: Moves attributes and attribute folders (with their contents) into the target folder, which must be of the same attribute type; an empty target path is the root folder. Returns one execution result per attribute and per folder. Available from Archicad 26.

Attribute Commands.name: MoveGraphicOverrideRules
Attribute Commands.description: Moves graphic override rules to another rule group, or to another place in their own group. Available from Archicad 27.

Attribute Commands.name: RenameAttributeFolders
Attribute Commands.description: Renames attribute folders, each given by attribute type and path, to the given new names. The root folder cannot be renamed. Available from Archicad 26.

Attribute Commands.name: RenameGraphicOverrideRuleGroups
Attribute Commands.description: Renames graphic override rule groups, found by name. Their rules are kept. Available from Archicad 27.

Classification Commands.name: CreateClassificationItems
Classification Commands.description: Creates Classification Items in the given Classification Systems based on the given parameters.

Classification Commands.name: CreateClassificationSystems
Classification Commands.description: Creates Classification Systems including Classification Items based on the given parameters.

Classification Commands.name: GetClassificationsOfElementDefaults
Classification Commands.description: Returns the classification of the tool defaults (the settings new elements get) of the given element types in the given classification systems.

Classification Commands.name: GetClassificationsOfElements
Classification Commands.description: Returns the classification of the given elements in the given classification systems. It works for subelements of hierarchal elements also.

Classification Commands.name: ImportClassificationsXml
Classification Commands.description: Imports a Classification Manager XML export, with the given policies for systems and items that already exist. Returns the systems and items it created and removed.

Classification Commands.name: SetClassificationsOfElementDefaults
Classification Commands.description: Sets the classifications of the tool defaults (the settings new elements get) of the given element types. In order to set a default to unclassified, omit the classificationItemId field.

Classification Commands.name: SetClassificationsOfElements
Classification Commands.description: Sets the classifications of elements. In order to set the classification of an element to unclassified, omit the classificationItemId field. It works for subelements of hierarchal elements also.

Classification Commands.name: UpdateClassificationItems
Classification Commands.description: Updates the id (code), name and/or description of existing Classification Items, keeping their guid and so the elements classified with them. Items cannot be moved to another parent.

Classification Commands.name: UpdateClassificationSystems
Classification Commands.description: Updates the name, description, source, version and/or date of existing Classification Systems, keeping their guid.

Design Options Commands.name: CreateDesignOptionCombinations
Design Options Commands.description: Creates new design option combinations with the given parameters. Available from Archicad 29.

Design Options Commands.name: CreateDesignOptionSets
Design Options Commands.description: Creates new design option sets with the given names. Available from Archicad 29.

Design Options Commands.name: CreateDesignOptions
Design Options Commands.description: Creates new design options with the given parameters. Available from Archicad 29.

Design Options Commands.name: DeactivateDesignOptionsInCombinations
Design Options Commands.description: Turns off the given design options in the given combinations, leaving their other options as they are. Available from Archicad 29.

Design Options Commands.name: DeleteDesignOptionCombinations
Design Options Commands.description: Deletes the given design option combinations. Available from Archicad 29.

Design Options Commands.name: DeleteDesignOptionSets
Design Options Commands.description: Deletes the given design option sets. Available from Archicad 29.

Design Options Commands.name: DeleteDesignOptions
Design Options Commands.description: Deletes the given design options. Available from Archicad 29.

Design Options Commands.name: DuplicateDesignOptionCombinations
Design Options Commands.description: Duplicates the given design option combinations and returns the identifiers of the new combinations. Available from Archicad 29.

Design Options Commands.name: GetDesignOptionCombinations
Design Options Commands.description: Retrieves information about existing design option combinations.

Design Options Commands.name: GetDesignOptionForElements
Design Options Commands.description: Retrieves the design option association for the specified elements. Available from Archicad 29.

Design Options Commands.name: GetDesignOptionSets
Design Options Commands.description: Retrieves information about existing design option sets, and in Teamwork projects the Teamwork identifier of the design options. Available from Archicad 29.

Design Options Commands.name: GetDesignOptions
Design Options Commands.description: Retrieves information about existing design options. Available from Archicad 29.

Design Options Commands.name: GetElementsOfDesignOptions
Design Options Commands.description: Retrieves the elements associated with the given design options. Available from Archicad 29.

Design Options Commands.name: MoveDesignOptionsToAnotherSet
Design Options Commands.description: Moves the given design options to another sets. Available from Archicad 29.

Design Options Commands.name: MoveElementsToDesignOptions
Design Options Commands.description: Moves the given elements into the given design options. Use NULLGuid for design option to remove the element from any design options and move it to the main model. Available from Archicad 29.

Design Options Commands.name: RenameDesignOptionCombinations
Design Options Commands.description: Changes the name of the given design option combinations. Available from Archicad 29.

Design Options Commands.name: RenameDesignOptionSets
Design Options Commands.description: Changes the name of the given design option sets. Available from Archicad 29.

Design Options Commands.name: RenameDesignOptions
Design Options Commands.description: Changes the name and/or the string id of the given design options. Available from Archicad 29.

Design Options Commands.name: SetActiveDesignOptionsInCombinations
Design Options Commands.description: Sets active design options in the given combinations. Available from Archicad 29.

Graphic Override Commands.name: CreateGraphicalOverrideCombination
Graphic Override Commands.description: Creates a graphic override combination from rule names, or replaces the rules of an existing one. Needs Archicad 27 or later.

Graphic Override Commands.name: CreateGraphicalOverrideRule
Graphic Override Commands.description: Creates or overwrites a graphic override rule in a rule group: name, criterion XML, surface color and line pen. Needs Archicad 27 or later.

Graphic Override Commands.name: GetGraphicalOverrideRules
Graphic Override Commands.description: Returns every graphic override rule with its criterion XML. Needs Archicad 27 or later.

Element grouping Commands.name: CreateGroups
Element grouping Commands.description: Creates groups of the passed elements

Element grouping Commands.name: GetElementSetsOfElements
Element grouping Commands.description: Gets the element sets that contain each given element. Only element sets created by the Tapir Add-On are examined; sets created by other add-ons are not found.

Element grouping Commands.name: GetElementsOfGroups
Element grouping Commands.description: Gets the elements directly contained by each given group.

Element grouping Commands.name: GetGroupsOfElements
